chapter: Arriving in New York and founding the Afro-Cubans
title: Top billing trick and taking over the Park Plaza
summary: Machito put his name on top of the bill, won the crowd, and when Montecino left for another job, the band got the Park Plaza.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: He just - I-didn't bother because I wanted to get at him; as a matter of fact, I did a trick. He had - his dance was postponed so he say: "Gee, my dance was postponed, I want to play here this coming Saturday". I said, why don't we put the two bands together? He said: "No, no, no, no, if you put your band, you are responsible the expenses your band and I responsible for mine, so if you want to play together you got to pay for your band." I said, okay, so we went together to the, to the printer and I say, in order to get top billing, I say: "Machito declare war to the best timbales player in the whole world, Montecino and his Happy Boys", but my name was on top, "Machito declare War", imagine, like Machito declare war to Count Basie. You understand? Right there I'm getting top billing, but he didn't realize because I called him the king of the timbales, so he didn't realize that I was tricking; (Chuckle) so when we went to the Park Plaza, the people that was fed-up with his nonchalance attitude, lateness], sometimes they postponed the Sunday dance and went to play with Cugat, to with Cugat and Duke Ellington, $o right there the owner of the place was fed-up too with the Happy Boys. So the people

they was fed up so when we played, we were the first ones to start. We start with "Intermezzo" and the "Muerto se fue de Rumba". We were rehearsong with a good sound, so imagine!, we got there with uniforms, because everything was prepared to giving a good impression.

I remember we had a tan - a dark-tan jacket - with a light-tan gabardine and white and brown shoes, beautiful! and they was clean too, but we had dark shoes, you know, so we were just dressed for Sunday; there was a reflection look on Sunday;/ and all, you know, all the guys, you know, you know how the neighborhood guys are. They were so mad about them that we stop playing, they say: "Hey, Machito, no, one more, one more time, Machito", so the owner of the place listen to the reaction of my band and they said "now I have, I have the guy that could replace this fellow"; but he didn't tell me anything, so the next Sunday, that was Easter Sunday, and Montecino went to play at the St. Nicholas Arena - that was a ballroom in those days - with Xavier Cugat, and he left flat the Park Plaza.

He had my phone, the same number that Mario had, Monument 2-6641, so he called Mario and in account that everybody was living in the same neighborhood, we put together the band in fifteen minutes, so we went to the Park Plaza and is, is a history. He didn't want no more Happy Boys and nobody but Machito and then we used the place, we owned the door, we charged fifty cents and twenty-five cents the women. In those days the scale was seven dollars so sometimes Monday, we got to go to the pawn shop to pawn a suit
or a pair of shoes in order to pay the musicians. You know, struggling like, like anybody else.
